companyIntro.name: Atlas Manufacturing
companyIntro.mission: World-class manufacturing discipline — every defect has a root cause, and every root cause gets fixed once, not patched repeatedly.
companyIntro.culture: Lean-first and data-driven. Line staff and engineers alike are expected to know their process' current defect rate from memory.

projectBackground.name: Pump Reliability Programme
projectBackground.context: Unplanned pump failures are the biggest cause of downtime. Maintenance asks where to focus first.

manager.name: Soo-jin Han
manager.note: Don't maintain everything equally. Find what fails, what it costs and what you can prevent.

assignment.title: Target the worst pumps
assignment.brief: Compute MTBF and availability, rank assets in Excel, choose strategies and write the maintenance recommendation.

documents.name: Failure Data
documents.note: 2,400 operating hours with 6 failures on one pump; average repair 8 hours.

documents.name: Asset Register
documents.note: Three pumps with hours, failures and repair times.

tasks.title: MTBF
tasks.prompt: A pump ran 2,400 hours with 6 failures. What is MTBF (hours)?
tasks.reasoning: MTBF is operating time over failures.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Availability
tasks.prompt: MTBF is 400 h and MTTR is 8 h. Availability = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR). What is it (%)?
tasks.reasoning: Availability combines how often and how long.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Maintenance Strategy
tasks.prompt: A pump has random failures and low-cost spare. A critical pump has wear that vibration monitoring can detect. Best strategy for the critical pump?
tasks.reasoning: Condition-based maintenance acts on evidence of deterioration.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Cost Logic
tasks.prompt: A planned repair costs £2,000 and a failure £15,000. A failure is expected twice a year without it. What does it suggest?
tasks.reasoning: Expected failure cost of £30,000 exceeds prevention cost.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Asset Reliability (Excel)
tasks.prompt: MTBF (E = B / C) and availability % (F = E / (E + D) x 100). Upload for checking.
tasks.reasoning: P2 is the worst performer: lowest MTBF and availability.
tasks.mistake: Treating all pumps alike wastes effort.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Maintenance Recommendation
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence recommendation on where to focus first.
tasks.modelAnswer: Pump P2 has the lowest MTBF (250 h) and availability (96.15%), so it deserves the first reliability review: root cause analysis of its 8 failures and a vibration monitoring trial. P1 and P3 can stay on current preventive schedules. With failures costing £15,000 against £2,000 planned work, prevention pays back quickly. I will report MTBF and availability monthly to confirm the improvement.
tasks.reasoning: A good recommendation ranks assets, proposes actions and justifies with cost.
tasks.mistake: Treating every asset alike spreads effort too thin.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Fix-It-Again Pump
caseStudy.background: A pump failed every two months and was repaired each time without root cause analysis. A bearing misalignment was finally found after 14 failures and £210,000 of downtime.
caseStudy.challenges: Repairs were treated as the end of the job.
questions: What would you do after the second failure?
How should repeat failures be flagged?
caseStudy.solution: Atlas triggered mandatory root cause analysis after any repeat failure within 90 days.

prompts: Which asset would you attack first and why?
How do you decide between preventive and condition-based?
